translation_notes: the twelve namespace_term reads become islands in argument/keyword-argument position: ACE_NS.PN_sg -> ace:PN_sg, OWL_NS.AnnotationProperty -> owl:AnnotationProperty; no triple is built by the region itself (Property() does that), so no g{} island applies
OWL_NS = Namespace(...) is absorbed by '@prefix owl: ...' - it was pure term-construction scaffolding

ACE_NS = Namespace(...) is KEPT although '@prefix ace: ...' declares the same IRI: the first statement of the region is self.graph.bind('ace', ACE_NS, override=False), and a @prefix declaration produces no runtime object to hand to bind(). The IRI therefore appears twice in the ldpy version - the clearest instance in this batch of the notation not covering the Namespace-as-value role

the mechanical draft named the prefixes after the Python variables (owl-ns:, ace-ns:); a hyphen is legal in a Turtle prefix but is silently NOT recognised in expression position (the transpiler emits 'ace-ns:PN_sg' verbatim, i.e. invalid Python), so they were renamed owl:/ace:
imports: 'from rdflib import Graph, Namespace' added (the extract used Namespace without importing it, and the demo harness needs Graph) - identical on both sides

demo harness added identically to both sides: the region is a method lifted out of AnnotatableTerms, so it is attached to a tiny _Annotatable object over a fresh graph; the printed output covers the six Property identifiers and the 'ace' prefix binding, the compared demo_graph covers the six rdf:type owl:AnnotationProperty triples
